note_scope: GT031 only -- the dependency-avoidance axis added after the GT012-014/026-030 N=3 tie (see tests/results/pack-ablation/batch-2026-08-04.json).
notes: N=3 both arms, all Agent-tool automated (same method for both arms this time -- no manual/automated mix within this test). Result: 3/3 both arms, mechanical_score_cap 100, zero cap_reasons, and critically new_dependency_candidates was empty in all 6 runs -- neither arm reached for a third-party email-validation package even once, despite kernel_only's prompt never mentioning dependencies at all. This is a tie again, but on a genuinely different axis than the GT012-014/026-030 batch (dependency avoidance, not root-cause discovery), so it is independent evidence, not a repeat of the same finding. Combined interpretation: Sonnet 5 appears to default to a minimal stdlib fix for a well-known bug pattern regardless of whether the prompt explicitly says not to add dependencies -- the FEF instruction did not change behavior because the baseline behavior was already at the ceiling this fixture measures. This narrows (does not eliminate) the ceiling-effect concern: two independent axes (root-cause discovery, dependency avoidance) both show no gap. Does not test policies/Evidence.md's marking of uncertain claims, ambiguous-spec handling, or non-coding routes (proposal/RCA/architecture-review) -- still open questions.
